title: Evidence
content:
Evidence

A result is measured only after a real deploy on that plan and a test. A documentation page alone is not a measurement. A third-party claim is not a measurement.

The ledger is docs/results.md. Each row is one deploy and one test run. Columns include plan, date (UTC), Wrangler, command, and result. A failed deploy stays in the table. A later row may correct an earlier row. The earlier row stays.

Conformance comes before performance. The upstream WordPress, WooCommerce, and Gutenberg test suites decide what works means.

What to read first

  • Install rows (2026-11-24): b-dosql, Workers for Platforms, and approach A Pass from main.
  • Load and concurrency: cached guests vs uncached PHP; A vs b-dosql isolate counts.
  • Conformance: WordPress and WooCommerce suites on named sites (cf759hw, cf759hl, cf759p, cf759a).
  • docs/conformance.md -- how a conformance run treats credentials and traces.
  • docs/perf-dosql.md -- what sets b-dosql's uncached limit.

Figures we cite on this site

  • Cached guest reads: about 26 to 30 req/s per site, p50 near 200 ms (docs/load-152.md, 2026-11-08).
  • b-dosql uncached: about 5 req/s; refuse near 100 clients (perf-dosql.md).
  • b-dosql Woo under load: 43 isolate resets and 49 lost writes per 1000 server requests on cf759a (2026-11-22).
  • Approach A WordPress: wp 18/18; routes.py 0 failures on cf759hw (2026-11-20).
  • Approach A WooCommerce: tests/woo.py 12/12, three runs (2026-11-09).
  • Approach A concurrency: up to 118 isolates at 50 concurrent users (2026-11-09).
  • Workers Paid $5/mo; WfP path $30/mo at rest for two or more sites (cost.md, read 2026-11-06).

Live examples

  • ggc.sh -- WooCommerce store on this framework. Guest storefront can be cached. Cart, checkout, account, and logged-in pages always run PHP.
  • www.pagefeather.dev -- this marketing site, a b-dosql WordPress deploy on Workers Paid (MEDIA=1, WooCommerce off).
